categoryNote: Foundation category: consumer-content suppression, notification defaults, background-app policy, search surfaces, update/maintenance ergonomics, component and default-app management. Evidence discipline: E1 entries cite Microsoft-documented policy values verified on learn.microsoft.com and in the local build-26300 ADMX files (2026-11-23); E0 entries are community-known value families whose exact names were verified read-only on a live 26300 profile. Every HKCU value is journaled with value-existence flags and affects the current user profile only; NEXTRIX v1 never loads the Default user hive (coordinator-level design decision).

tweaks.name: Disable Windows tips & suggestions
tweaks.description: Turns off Windows tips, soft-landing prompts and system-pane suggestions for the current user.
tweaks.objective: Remove the per-user tips and suggestion content stream Windows delivers through the ContentDeliveryManager store.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Sets three DWORD values to 0 under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager: SubscribedContent-338388Enabled (tips), SoftLandingEnabled (soft-landing prompts) and SystemPaneSuggestionsEnabled (system-pane suggestions) - the family Sophia Script groups as its WindowsTips function (r5). Per-user scope: values affect the invoking user profile only and are journaled with key- and value-existence flags; new user profiles keep Windows defaults until the entry is applied for them. NEXTRIX v1 does not load the Default user hive (coordinator-level design decision; the XOS NTUSER.DAT reg-load pattern recorded in r1 is deliberately not adopted here). Evidence E0: the value family is community-known (r5) and Microsoft does not document these values, but all three value names were verified present on a live build-26300 profile read-only (2026-11-23).
tweaks.defaultState: Tips and suggestions allowed; values are typically absent or 1 depending on build, edition and OOBE choices (exact per-profile defaults vary).
tweaks.proposedState: SubscribedContent-338388Enabled=0, SoftLandingEnabled=0, SystemPaneSuggestionsEnabled=0 (DWord) for the current user.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState (NxVerify) confirms each value is DWord 0 after apply; one journal verify entry per value.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original value and kind; values that never existed are deleted; only-if-ours divergence is reported, never clobbered.

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value (keyExisted, existed, kind, value) journaled before any mutation.

sideEffects: Windows tips and suggestion content no longer appear for the current user.
Other and future user profiles are unaffected (per-user scope).
documentationSource: Live read-only value-name verification on build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.technicalExplanation: Sets SubscribedContent-310093Enabled=0 (DWord) under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\ContentDeliveryManager for the current user (community-known family per r5, value verified present on a live build-26300 profile read-only, 2026-11-23). Honest evidence split: a Microsoft-documented User-scope policy exists for the same feature (DisableWindowsSpotlightWindowsWelcomeExperience, CloudContent.admx, 'Turn off the Windows Welcome Experience', User Configuration; verified on the Policy CSP Experience page and in the local CloudContent.admx, which declares class="User"), but Microsoft documents its MDM surface for Enterprise/Education editions only - NEXTRIX targets Home/Pro as well, so the community-known per-user CDM value is the applied mechanism and the documented policy analog is recorded here for Enterprise/Education owners who prefer the policy surface. Per-user scope only; Default-hive handling is a coordinator-level decision (NX01-001 note).
tweaks.defaultState: Welcome experience allowed; value absent or 1 depending on profile history.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms SubscribedContent-310093Enabled is DWord 0 after apply.

Documented policy analog (Enterprise/Education) not written by this entry.

tweaks.name: Disable consumer experience / suggested apps
tweaks.description: Applies the documented 'Turn off Microsoft consumer experiences' policy machine-wide.
tweaks.objective: Suppress Microsoft consumer content delivery (suggested apps, membership notifications, post-OOBE installs and redirect tiles) at the documented policy layer.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Writes the documented ADMX policy value DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures=1 (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent. Verified 2026-11-23: the Policy CSP Experience page maps AllowWindowsConsumerFeatures to registry key Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent, value name DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures, CloudContent.admx ('Turn off Microsoft consumer experiences', Computer Configuration), and the local CloudContent.admx on build 26300 declares the policy class="Machine" with that exact key and value name. Machine-wide at the policy layer, including profiles created later; the HKCU ContentDeliveryManager families (NX01-001/002/004/005) remain per-user and separately journaled - this entry deliberately writes no HKCU value (anti-duplication). Honest applicability: the CSP edition row marks the MDM surface Enterprise/Education/IoT only (Pro excluded from that CSP), while the ADMX policy is present in Pro's Group Policy surface and community consensus (WinUtil WPFTweaksConsumerFeatures with <RemoveEntry> undo semantics, r5) reports it effective on Pro; capability detection stays primary and Home is excluded honestly (no documented policy surface).
tweaks.defaultState: Consumer features allowed; policy value absent (policy key typically absent).
tweaks.proposedState: DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures=1 (DWord) at the machine policy layer.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures is DWord 1 after apply; gpedit shows the policy enabled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the journaled original (or removes the value if it never existed - WinUtil <RemoveEntry> semantics, r5).

tweaks.name: Disable Start menu suggestions
tweaks.description: Turns off the Start menu suggestion/tips content families (23H2-era CDM value and 24H2+ Explorer value), capability-checked.
tweaks.objective: Suppress promotional suggestions delivered into the Start menu without touching the recommendations section itself.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Build-conditional, capability-checked layers (both journaled separately): (1) 23H2-era family - CDM SubscribedContent-338389Enabled=0 under HKCU\...\ContentDeliveryManager (community-known; value verified present on build 26300 read-only); (2) 24H2+ family - Explorer\Advanced Start_IrisRecommendations=0 under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced ('Show recommendations for tips, app shortcuts and more'; value verified present on build 26300 read-only). Each action declares a capabilityPath, so a missing family skips gracefully with a reason instead of fabricating state (architecture section 4: never create unsupported keys). Boundary honesty (mechanism-owner rule): the Start menu Recommended section content itself (Start_TrackDocs/Start_TrackProgs families - recent files/app pins) belongs to NX15-005 and is NOT touched here; Start_AccountNotifications exists in the same 24H2 Start family on build 26300 but is deliberately not claimed by this entry - flagged to the coordinator for adjudication with NX15-005. KB5089573 may remove legacy Start code paths (COMPATIBILITY_RESEARCH section 2) - hence the capability gates and per-action journaling rather than a build assumption.
tweaks.defaultState: Start suggestions allowed; values absent or 1 depending on build and profile history.
tweaks.proposedState: SubscribedContent-338389Enabled=0 (CDM layer) and Start_IrisRecommendations=0 (Explorer layer, where present).

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms each applied value is DWord 0; skipped layers are reported with the capability reason.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original value/kind per layer (or deletes values that never existed).

tweaks.name: Notification defaults configuration
tweaks.description: Establishes sane notification defaults: per-user toasts enabled, lock-screen message previews off via the documented WPN policy.
tweaks.objective: A coherent notification baseline: notifications work, but personal message content does not appear on the lock screen.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Two journaled layers with honest evidence split. (1) Per-user toast master: ToastEnabled=1 (DWord) on the real settings key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\PushNotifications - a community-known value behind Settings > System > Notifications (E0); per Sophia's policy-vs-real-key hygiene (r5) the real key is used rather than a policy key so the state stays visible in Settings UI; value verified present read-only on build 26300. This re-arms notifications as a foundation default; users who deliberately want no toasts should deselect this entry (their prior state is restored on rollback). (2) Documented policy: NoToastApplicationNotificationOnLockScreen=1 (DWord) on the User-class policy path HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\PushNotifications - 'Turn off toast notifications on the lock screen', WPN.admx, class="User" (verified on the ADMX_WPN Policy CSP page and in the local WPN.admx, 2026-11-23). Entry evidence is E1 because layer (2) is Microsoft-documented; layer (1) is labeled E0. Both values are HKCU, so the tweak needs no elevation for its own actions (materials in an elevated session still resolve to the invoking user's hive - coordinator note). Trade-off stated: lock-screen toast previews disappear until undone.
tweaks.defaultState: Notifications allowed per user; lock-screen toasts allowed; policy value absent.
tweaks.proposedState: ToastEnabled=1 (per-user master) and NoToastApplicationNotificationOnLockScreen=1 (User-class policy) for the current user.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms both values are DWord as proposed; Settings > System > Notifications reflects the toast state.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original (deletes policy value if it never existed - policy-off semantics).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value journaled before mutation (policy-key existence recorded separately from the real key).

sideEffects: Lock-screen toast previews stop for the current user.
Users who had deliberately disabled all notifications get them re-enabled by layer (1) - deselect this entry if that is your intent.
documentationSource: Live read-only value-name verification on build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Global UWP background-app permission policy
tweaks.description: Sets the global 'apps can run in the background' default: per-user global toggle plus an optional documented device policy.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner a journaled global switch for Windows-app background execution, without touching per-app permissions.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxBackgroundAppsGlobal (src/nxcore/functions/NX01.ps1), two journaled layers: (1) per-user global toggle GlobalUserDisabled=1 (DWord) under HKCU\...\BackgroundAccessApplications - community-known (E0), value name verified present read-only on build 26300; (2) optional documented device policy LetAppsRunInBackground=2 ('Force deny') under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\AppPrivacy - AppPrivacy.admx, 'Let Windows apps run in the background' (verified on the Policy CSP Privacy page and in the local AppPrivacy.admx; enum 0=user in control, 1=force allow, 2=force deny), applied only with -IncludeDevicePolicy. Every value write follows the pipeline: Capture-NxRegistryValue -> Add-NxJournalEntry -> Set-NxRegistryValue -> Test-NxConfigurationState -> journaled result; already-correct values journal a 'skip' (AlreadyApplied) and are not rewritten (idempotent). Honest breakage record: ReviOS revert.yml withdrew a background-apps disable because it 'breaks Xbox Game Bar KGL update' (r2) - hence CONDITIONAL, Streamer profile (P4) excluded, confirmation required. Microsoft's own CSP warning is recorded verbatim in effect: communication apps lose tile/notification updates and background mail sync may stop (verified CSP text, 2026-11-23). Per-app background permissions are NX11-002's mechanism (XREF); this entry never writes the AppPrivacy per-app override lists (LetAppsRunInBackground_ForceAllowTheseApps etc., verified present in local AppPrivacy.admx - recorded for NX11-002 integration).
tweaks.defaultState: No global toggle set (GlobalUserDisabled absent = apps may run in background subject to per-app/user settings); policy value absent.
tweaks.proposedState: GlobalUserDisabled=1 per user; optionally LetAppsRunInBackground=2 at the device policy layer.

verify.procedure: Function re-reads each written value via Test-NxConfigurationState and journals a verify entry; report lists layers applied/skipped and the app-restart note.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores journaled originals (registry targets); the function itself is idempotent so re-running with -Mode Enable writes the documented 'user in control'/0 state and journals it.

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per layer (keyExisted, existed, kind, value) journaled before mutation; policy-key existence recorded separately.

sideEffects: Background apps stop updating tiles/notifications; background mail/voicemail sync may stop (Microsoft CSP warning).
Xbox Game Bar KGL update breakage is documented for global background-app disables (ReviOS revert.yml, r2) - Streamer profile excluded, confirmation required.
Open apps must be restarted to pick up the policy (Microsoft CSP text).
documentationSource: Live read-only value-name verification on build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Windows Search indexing scope configuration
tweaks.description: Documented scope-management design for the Windows Search index (defined, not applied in engine v0.1); read-only inventory helper ships in the module.
tweaks.objective: Own indexing SCOPE (what gets indexed) with documented mechanisms only, leaving service configuration to NX11-008.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Defined with an honest limitation, per the catalogue's cleanliness bar. The documented scope mechanisms are: (1) the CrawlScopeManager COM API of the Windows Search platform (ICrawlScopeManager AddDefaultScopeRule/RemoveScopeRule, Windows Search API documentation) - implementing it requires COM interop whose exact interface GUIDs/vtable order cannot be verified safely read-only, and a mis-declared vtable risks instability; not cleanly implementable without owner-hardware validation, so NEXTRIX v1 does not ship a mutation path; (2) documented narrow Search.admx policies that ARE registry-based and cleanly implementable as declarative follow-ups if the owner wants a narrow v1: DisableRemovableDriveIndexing (registry value name verified in local Search.admx, searchable by capability) and AllowFindMyFiles (Find My Files scope toggle, documented on the Search CSP page). Raw writes to the CrawlScopeManager WorkingSet\Rules registry mirror are NOT a documented write path and are rejected (architecture section 4: never create unsupported keys to make a tweak 'appear applied'). Boundary: the WSearch service configuration belongs to NX11-008 (XREF); SSD/HDD indexing parameters are NX06 guidance (XREF); this entry owns scope only. The module ships the read-only Get-NxSearchCrawlScopeInventory helper (service status read-only, documented policy values, rule-mirror enumeration for inspection) so the owner can capture the current scope before any future mutation design.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default indexing scope (user profile/content locations, per Windows Search defaults); no NEXTRIX scope policy applied.
tweaks.proposedState: Owner-selected excluded paths/scopes applied through documented mechanisms (not applied in engine v0.1 - entry defined).

verify.procedure: Get-NxSearchCrawlScopeInventory reports current scope/policy state before and after any future mutation; engine v0.1 reports this action as NotImplemented (defined, not applied).

rollback.procedure: Not applicable in v0.1 - no mutation path is shipped; any future implementation must journal per-rule scope changes and restore them via the same documented API.

originalState.method: Read-only inventory (Get-NxSearchCrawlScopeInventory) captures the current scope for the record; no mutation exists yet.

sideEffects: None in v0.1 (defined only). Future scope exclusions would reduce search coverage for the excluded paths.
documentationSource: Windows Search API documentation, ICrawlScopeManager (learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/search; deep link not verified this session and thus not cited)
Catalogue XREF: NX11-008 (WSearch service), NX06 (SSD/HDD guidance)

tweaks.objective: Remove the rotating promotional/seasonal content from the search surface.

(1) Documented policy: EnableDynamicContentInWSB=0 (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Search - the AllowSearchHighlights policy ('Allow search highlights', Search.admx; CSP text: disabling 'turns off search highlights in search home, and the taskbar search box (Windows 10) or the Start menu search box (Windows 11)'; applicable Windows 11 22H2+, within NEXTRIX's 23H2+ floor). Verified on the Policy CSP Search page and in the local Search.admx (value name EnableDynamicContentInWSB), 2026-11-23. (2) Per-user community value named by the catalogue: IsDynamicSearchBoxEnabled=0 (DWord) under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\SearchSettings - E0, value verified present read-only on build 26300; kept as a journaled secondary layer so per-user state is also captured/restored. Evidence note: the catalogue desk assignment was E0; the entry is recorded E1 because the documented AllowSearchHighlights policy covers the same feature (mission's documented-policy exception), with the E0 layer explicitly labeled. Mixed layers: policy writes need elevation (entry privileges Admin); the HKCU layer resolves to the invoking user in an elevated session.

tweaks.name: Delivery Optimization configuration
tweaks.description: Sets the documented Delivery Optimization download mode (default proposal: HTTP only, peer sharing off).
tweaks.objective: Put Delivery Optimization behavior under an explicit, documented, journaled policy without disabling the DO service.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Writes the documented 'Download Mode' policy DODownloadMode=0 (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeliveryOptimization (DeliveryOptimization.admx; verified on learn.microsoft.com 'Delivery Optimization reference' and in the local ADMX, 2026-11-23). Proposed default 0 = HTTP only: DO stays enabled with its cloud metadata and cache, but peer-to-peer download/upload is off. Mode menu for owner choice before apply (documented): 0 HTTP-only (proposed), 1 LAN peers (Windows default), 2 Group, 3 Internet, 99 Simple (offline); Bypass=100 is deprecated in Windows 11 and must not be configured (explicit Microsoft guidance). Trade-off: no peer-sourced update bytes and no upstream upload; LAN reuse of downloaded content is lost - owners who prefer peer sharing should keep 1 or choose 2/3. The documented bandwidth family (DOMaxBackgroundDownloadBandwidth, DOPercentageMaxForegroundBandwidth, business-hour variants - all on the reference page) exists for parameterized follow-ups and is not written by this default action. DoSvc itself is on NEXTRIX's never-touch service list (registry/schema.json) and is never disabled, stopped or reconfigured - configuration is policy-only. Edition note (house rule Section 6): Home is excluded here because this entry is written against the policy surface documented for Pro/Enterprise/Education; Home enforcement is not separately documented - no undocumented Home claim is made.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default mode LAN (1): peer sharing on the local network; policy value absent (or whatever a managed environment set).
tweaks.proposedState: DODownloadMode=0 (HTTP only) at the machine policy layer.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms DODownloadMode is DWord 0 after apply; Get-DeliveryOptimizationStatus reflects the mode (owner-run).

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the journaled original (removes the value if it never existed, returning to the Windows default).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue (keyExisted, existed, kind, value) journaled before mutation; policy-key existence recorded separately.

sideEffects: No peer-shared update downloads/uploads while set to 0.
LAN update-content reuse lost; HTTP downloads remain (documented mode semantics).

tweaks.name: Automatic maintenance schedule
tweaks.description: Keeps Automatic Maintenance enabled but prevents it from waking the machine (documented WakeUp policy).
tweaks.objective: State and configure the maintenance wake-time trade-off without disabling maintenance or its tasks.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Writes the documented 'Automatic Maintenance WakeUp Policy' WakeUp=0 (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Task Scheduler\Maintenance (msched.admx; verified on the Policy CSP Update page - AutomaticMaintenanceWakeUp maps to that key and value, 0=Disabled/1=Enabled - and in the local msched.admx, 2026-11-23). Trade-off stated: Automatic Maintenance stays fully enabled (NEXTRIX never disables maintenance tasks or updates - update starvation is a rejected pattern, RESEARCH_RECONCILIATION REJECT register), but it will not wake the machine for the daily window; maintenance runs at the next idle opportunity instead, so on machines that are rarely idle at the boundary time it can drift into active hours. Adjacent documented policies (recorded, not written): ActivationBoundaryPolicy ('Activation Boundary' value - verified in local msched.admx) and RandomDelayPolicy ('Randomized'/'Random Delay' values); the CSP reference does not document the accepted value format for the boundary string, so v1 deliberately does not write them rather than invent a data format - owners needing a specific boundary time set it in gpedit and NEXTRIX's journal remains the rollback record for the values it wrote. Live read-only check on build 26300: the real maintenance key values are absent (Windows defaults apply), so defaultState is recorded from that observation. Edition note (house rule Section 6): Home is excluded here because the maintenance policy surface is documented for Pro/Enterprise/Education; Home enforcement is not separately documented.
tweaks.defaultState: Values absent on a stock 26300 root key (verified read-only 2026-11-23): Windows default maintenance cadence, wake behavior per Control Panel 'Automatic Maintenance' setting.
tweaks.proposedState: WakeUp=0 (DWord) at the policy layer; maintenance fully enabled, no wake requests.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms WakeUp is DWord 0; Security and Maintenance still reports Automatic Maintenance enabled.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores the journaled original (removes the value if it never existed, returning to Control-Panel behavior).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue (keyExisted, existed, kind, value) journaled before mutation; policy-key existence recorded separately.

sideEffects: Maintenance no longer wakes the machine (good for laptop bags/bedroom machines); it can drift into active hours on machines that never idle at the window.
Maintenance and its tasks remain enabled - nothing is disabled.
documentationSource: Local msched.admx inspection and read-only maintenance-key check, build 26300 (2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Windows Update active hours configuration
tweaks.description: Pins a documented active-hours window so update restarts do not happen while the owner uses the machine.
tweaks.objective: Express the owner's usage window through the documented active-hours policy.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Writes the documented 'Turn off auto-restart for updates during active hours' policy: SetActiveHours=1, ActiveHoursStart=8, ActiveHoursEnd=17 (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate (WindowsUpdate.admx; verified on the Policy CSP Update page - ActiveHoursStart/ActiveHoursEnd, int 0-23, documented defaults 8/17, registry key Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate - and in the local WindowsUpdate.admx whose ActiveHours policy declares enable value SetActiveHours with enum elements ActiveHoursStart/ActiveHoursEnd; 2026-11-23). Owner-chosen window: the two time values are the proposed DEFAULTS from Microsoft's documentation - owners EDIT them to their actual usage window before apply; the entry's value is the documented mechanism plus journaling, not a preference. Constraint honesty: the documented maximum range is 18 hours (ActiveHoursMaxRange policy, range 8-18); invalid windows are skipped with a clear reason. Documented policy interplay: this policy has no effect when 'No auto-restart with logged-on users for scheduled automatic updates installations' or 'Always automatically restart at scheduled time' is enabled - surfaced as an eligibility warning (NxCompat warnings) rather than a hard gate, because the conflicting policies are machine state NEXTRIX does not own. Edition note (house rule Section 6): Home is excluded because the update-policy surface is documented for Pro/Enterprise/Education; Home enforcement is not separately documented.
tweaks.defaultState: No policy values (policy key typically absent); Windows uses user-selected or automatic (smart) active hours.
tweaks.proposedState: SetActiveHours=1, ActiveHoursStart=8, ActiveHoursEnd=17 (DWord) - owner edits the window before apply.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms the three values; windows longer than 18 hours fail verification as out-of-range and are reported.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original (removes values that never existed - policy-off semantics).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value journaled before mutation; policy-key existence recorded separately.

sideEffects: Active hours become machine-fixed for all users while set (the policy locks the window); restarts are deferred outside it.
Documented max window is 18 hours - overnight-heavy schedules cannot be fully covered by one window.

tweaks.name: Restart notification configuration
tweaks.description: Quiets update nag notifications while keeping restart warnings (documented UpdateNotificationLevel policy).
tweaks.objective: Reduce update-notification noise without hiding restart warnings, using the Windows-11-applicable documented policy.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Writes the documented modern policy 'Display options for update notifications': SetUpdateNotificationLevel=1 (enable) and UpdateNotificationLevel=1 (all notifications off EXCEPT restart warnings) (DWord) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate (WindowsUpdate.admx; verified on the Policy CSP Update page - UpdateNotificationLevel 0 default / 1 excluding restart warnings / 2 including restart warnings - and in the local WindowsUpdate.admx where the policy declares valueName SetUpdateNotificationLevel with enum element UpdateNotificationLevel; 2026-11-23). Proposed value 1 is the restart-safe middle option; value 2 hides restart warnings too and is recorded as the more aggressive choice with Microsoft's own security caution (users may become unaware of critical updates) - the entry stays CONDITIONAL and is never auto-applied. Active-hours adjacency (catalogue note): the CSP page documents the interplay with active hours (NX01-013) and update deadlines - recorded as an informational dependency, not a hard one. Honest legacy finding: the classic restart-warning schedule policies (ScheduleRestartWarning, ScheduleImminentRestartWarning, SetAutoRestartNotificationDisable) are marked by Microsoft as LEGACY and 'not applicable for Windows 11' (verified on the Update CSP page, 2026-11-23) - NEXTRIX deliberately does not write them; this entry uses only the modern policy. Edition note (house rule Section 6): Home is excluded because the documented policy surface lists Pro/Enterprise/Education; Home enforcement is not separately documented.
tweaks.defaultState: No policy values (policy key typically absent); default Windows Update notifications, including restart warnings.
tweaks.proposedState: SetUpdateNotificationLevel=1 and UpdateNotificationLevel=1 (DWord): notifications off, restart warnings kept.

verify.procedure: Test-NxConfigurationState confirms both values are DWord 1; gpedit shows 'Display options for update notifications' = notifications off excluding restart warnings.

rollback.procedure: Invoke-NxRollback restores each journaled original (removes values that never existed - policy-off semantics).

originalState.method: Capture-NxRegistryValue per value journaled before mutation.

sideEffects: Update-completion/tip notifications are suppressed; restart warnings still appear.
With value 2 (owner override) restart warnings disappear too - security caution recorded from Microsoft's CSP text.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-update (UpdateNotificationLevel; legacy restart-warning policies marked not applicable for Windows 11)

tweaks.name: Optional features & components management
tweaks.description: Read-only optional-feature inventory plus a selective, journaled enable/disable of individual Windows optional features.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner a documented CIM/DISM inventory and a per-feature, journaled state control.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxOptionalFeatureInventory (read-only) and Set-NxOptionalFeatureState (mutating) in src/nxcore/functions/NX01.ps1, using the documented DISM PowerShell cmdlets (Get-WindowsOptionalFeature / Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature / Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature, learn.microsoft.com Dism module). Per-feature journaling: original state is captured via Get-WindowsOptionalFeature and recorded as a 'feature' target descriptor (featureName, original state) before mutation; the setter then runs Enable/Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -NoRestart, re-reads the state, and journals the verified result - restart-pending states (EnablePending/DisablePending) are reported as verified-with-restart-pending, never silently as success. Idempotency: an already-desired state journals a 'skip' (AlreadyApplied) and is not rewritten. Honest rollback labeling: engine v0.1 restores registry targets only - feature rollback is a documented inverse re-invocation (Set-NxOptionalFeatureState with the opposite state, original state recorded in the journal) and is not claimed as engine-automatic; removing a feature may require installation media on some SKUs. DISM cmdlets require elevation and are known to break from PowerShell 7/MSIX contexts (COMPATIBILITY_RESEARCH section 2) - the module therefore targets Windows PowerShell 5.1 (its #Requires floor) and imports the Dism module explicitly. -NoRestart is always used; RestartNeeded from the DISM result objects (when present) is surfaced in the result and journal, and the entry's restart field is 'Reboot' only because restart-requiring features exist (e.g. Hyper-V), not as a blanket requirement.
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default optional-feature states; no NEXTRIX record.
tweaks.proposedState: Inventory produced; owner-selected features enabled/disabled with per-feature journal entries.

verify.procedure: Set-NxOptionalFeatureState re-reads the feature state after mutation and journals Verified (or Verified-RestartPending); inventory can be re-run to confirm.

rollback.procedure: Documented inverse re-invocation with the journaled original state (engine v0.1 does not auto-restore 'feature' targets - labeled honestly); some feature removals may require installation media.

originalState.method: Get-WindowsOptionalFeature state captured per feature and journaled as a 'feature' descriptor before mutation.

sideEffects: Disabling a feature removes its functionality and may require a reboot (or installation media to re-enable on some SKUs).
RestartRequiring features report RestartNeeded; no restart is forced in-session.
documentationSource: COMPATIBILITY_RESEARCH.md section 2 (DISM cmdlets from PS7/MSIX broken - use Windows PowerShell 5.1)

tweaks.name: Default application associations
tweaks.description: Exports current default app associations, imports an owner-chosen associations XML via the documented DISM path, and journals before/after artifacts.
tweaks.objective: Managed default application associations with an exportable pre-change state and a documented inverse.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Invoke-NxDefaultAppAssociations (src/nxcore/functions/NX01.ps1) using the documented DISM XML commands (learn.microsoft.com 'Export or Import Default Application Associations': dism /Online /Export-DefaultAppAssociations and /Import-DefaultAppAssociations). Flow: (1) pre-change export to the NEXTRIX backup set - the original-state artifact recorded in the journal; (2) import of the owner-chosen XML; (3) verification via DISM exit codes plus a post-import re-export and a set-diff count of association entries for the report. Idempotency: when the pre-change export is byte-identical to the chosen XML the import is skipped (journal 'AlreadyApplied', overridable with -Force). Honest rollback labeling: re-importing the pre-change export restores prior defaults (documented inverse); engine v0.1 does not auto-restore 'appAssociations' targets - labeled, not hidden. UCPD note (24H2+): direct writes to per-user UserChoice/association-protection surfaces are UCPD-protected; this entry deliberately uses the DISM XML path, which configures DEFAULTS consumed at profile creation / system level and does not write the protected per-user UserChoice keys - the supported path replaces any policy fallback, and no UCPD-bypassing value is touched anywhere in NEXTRIX. New-user note: imported defaults apply to new user profiles and system defaults; existing users' live choices are untouched, and NEXTRIX v1 does not load the Default user hive (coordinator-level design, same as the CDM entries).
tweaks.defaultState: Windows default application associations; no NEXTRIX export exists.
tweaks.proposedState: Pre-change associations exported to the backup set; owner-chosen XML imported as the default-association set; result journaled.

verify.procedure: DISM exit code 0 plus a post-import re-export; diff count of association entries reported and journaled.

rollback.procedure: Re-import the journaled pre-change export (documented inverse). Engine v0.1 does not auto-restore 'appAssociations' targets - labeled honestly.

originalState.method: DISM pre-change export to the timestamped backup set; path + SHA256 journaled as the original-state descriptor.

sideEffects: New profiles get the imported defaults; per-user live choices are untouched (DISM XML semantics).
Import requires an owner-prepared XML exported from a machine whose associations are known-good.
documentationSource: COMPATIBILITY_RESEARCH.md section 2 (UCPD-protected per-user association values -> documented DISM path instead)
